solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Ruthlessly running clubs after top side demolished

indicators.note: after places the clubs letter at the end, following the rearranged letters
something demolished is knocked down to be rebuilt, so the letters of top side are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs

explanation.surface: A football club run with an iron fist after the top team is torn apart.
explanation.walkthrough: Topside is a cut of beef or a team's top side; here its letters are just fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A despotic ruler governs like a tyrant, so the word describes running things without mercy.

clue.text: For example, subject of sultan with a personality disorder

parts.note: e.g. is the abbreviation of exempli gratia
Oman is ruled by a sultan, so one of his subjects is an Omani
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sultan's subject is described as having a personality disorder.
explanation.walkthrough: Oman is a sultanate on the Arabian peninsula, so its people are subjects of a sultan.
explanation.definitionFit: Egomania is an obsessive self-absorption, treated as a disorder of the personality.

clue.text: Sign of equality in gymnastic event

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the equals sign is drawn as two level lines side by side
second meaning: the men's apparatus of two raised rails

explanation.walkthrough: The equals sign is literally two parallel bars, which is the joke behind pairing it with the gym apparatus.
explanation.definitionFit: The gymnastics apparatus has two horizontal rails, and the mathematical sign is two horizontal strokes.

clue.text: Type who believes, in a way, in what he is told

definitions.text: Type who believes, in a way

indicators.note: in tells us the answer lies inside the words that follow, spanning their letters

parts.note: the run of words that conceals the answer

explanation.surface: A person who has faith, in some sense, in whatever he is told.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'in' belongs to the definition's 'in a way'; the second is the signal that the answer sits inside the following words.
explanation.definitionFit: A theist believes in God, so is a type of believer in one particular way.

clue.text: It's worn over shoulders and head

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a sleeveless garment hanging from the shoulders
second meaning: a headland jutting into the sea

explanation.walkthrough: Shoulders and head suggest one body; the second word is a geographical headland.
explanation.definitionFit: A cape is both a cloak draped from the shoulders and a promontory, as in Cape Horn.

clue.text: Bizarre polemic Democrat put together

indicators.note: something bizarre is strangely twisted, so the letters of polemic are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A Democrat assembled a strange political attack.
explanation.definitionFit: To compile is to assemble material into a collection, which is putting it together.

clue.text: Foreigner at first without a right to a lawyer

indicators.note: without means the letter is dropped from the foreigner word
at first says the letter goes from the very start of the word

parts.note: an alien is a person from another country
taken as written

explanation.surface: A foreigner, at first, lacks the right to legal representation.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a right to counsel; the definition is a right as a lawyer sees it.
explanation.definitionFit: A lien is a legal right to keep someone's property until a debt is settled.

clue.text: Well positioned as player, pinching English forward's rear is not fair

indicators.note: pinching means catching hold of, so the English letter is held inside the other word

parts.note: a player is onside when legitimately placed, not offside

indicators.note: rear means the back end, so only the final letter of forward is used

parts.note: the word whose last letter is taken

explanation.surface: An onside player grabs an English forward's backside, which is hardly fair play.
explanation.walkthrough: Onside is the football and rugby term for being in a legal position on the field.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-sided contest or account favours one party unfairly, so it is unjust.

clue.text: For which a daughter's one possible choice?

definitions.text: For which a daughter's one possible choice?

parts.note: taken as written
an option is one of the choices available

explanation.surface: A question about the process by which a daughter is just one possible choice.
explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue describes adoption: parents may choose a daughter as one option; read in parts it builds the word.
explanation.definitionFit: In adoption a child, perhaps a daughter, is taken on by new parents as their own.

clue.text: Wild animal in ring kept in by stick

indicators.note: kept in by means held within, so the ring letter sits inside the stick word

parts.note: a bar is a rod or stick
O looks like a ring

explanation.surface: A wild beast in a circus ring is kept in place with a stick.
explanation.definitionFit: A boar is a wild pig, a classic quarry of the hunt.

clue.text: Arranged special calls for place in outback

indicators.note: arranged means put in a new order, so the letters of special are reshuffled

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
to ring someone is to phone, or call, them

explanation.surface: Someone sets up special phone calls to a remote spot in the Australian bush.
explanation.walkthrough: Ring is the British word for phoning, so calls gives rings.
explanation.definitionFit: Alice Springs is a town in Australia's Northern Territory, in the heart of the outback.

clue.text: Explorer that is getting anxious, initially, when trapped by bear, say

indicators.note: trapped by means caught inside, so the initials go within the bear word

parts.note: a bear is a stock-market investor who expects prices to fall

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of each of the words that come before it

parts.note: four words whose first letters are used

explanation.surface: An explorer grows nervous when cornered by a bear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that is' looks like i.e., but here only the initials of the four words count. A bear in finance is an investor betting on falling prices.
explanation.definitionFit: An investigator explores a matter, probing and searching it out like a detective.

clue.text: Part of house in end I idiotically blew up

indicators.note: in places the housing word inside the rearranged letters
done idiotically means done foolishly and out of order, so end and I are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
a flat is a set of rooms forming part of a building

explanation.surface: In the end, I foolishly blew up part of the house.
explanation.definitionFit: To inflate is to fill with air until it swells, so inflated means pumped up.

clue.text: Capital husband put into food business

indicators.note: put into means placed inside, so the husband letter goes within the food business

parts.note: a deli, short for delicatessen, sells prepared foods

explanation.surface: A husband is installed in a food business.
explanation.definitionFit: Delhi, strictly New Delhi, is the capital city of India.

clue.text: Imposed tax, say, and governed without struggle

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the governed word surrounds the struggle word

parts.note: to lead is to direct or govern
to vie is to compete or struggle

explanation.surface: A tax was imposed and the country was ruled without any fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like it means minus, but it means outside here.
explanation.definitionFit: A tax, duty or fine is levied when an authority imposes and collects it.

clue.text: China accepting you, it's said, as missionary

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the sound-alike letter goes inside the china word

parts.note: china is rhyming slang for mate (china plate), so a pal

indicators.note: it's said means spoken, so you is replaced by the letter that sounds the same

parts.note: the word that is said aloud

explanation.surface: A friend from China takes you in as a missionary.
explanation.walkthrough: In Cockney rhyming slang china plate means mate, so china is a pal.
explanation.definitionFit: St Paul was the great early Christian missionary whose journeys spread the gospel.

clue.text: Like euro for German, it's added to envelope

definitions.meaning: first meaning, read cryptically: the euro came after the Deutschmark, so it is the answer
second meaning: the franking stamp put on a letter by the post office

explanation.walkthrough: Germany's currency before the euro was the Deutschmark, so for Germans the euro is post-mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A postmark is the official stamp printed on mail showing date and place of posting.

clue.text: Legal volume needing a cover

parts.note: taken as written
a lid is a covering for a container

explanation.surface: A law book needs a binding.
explanation.definitionFit: Something valid is legally sound and binding, such as a valid contract.

clue.text: Source for some bars in a very unusual key

indicators.note: unusual means out of the ordinary arrangement, so in a very is reshuffled

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
taken as written, as anagram fodder
D is one of the musical keys

explanation.surface: Some bars of music are written in a very strange key.
explanation.walkthrough: The musical surface hides wine bars, which get their stock from where grapes are grown.
explanation.definitionFit: A vineyard grows grapes for wine, the stock of a wine bar.

clue.text: Oddly spoiled, so disposed of

indicators.note: oddly picks the odd-numbered letters, first, third, fifth and seventh

parts.note: the word whose odd letters are taken

explanation.surface: It had gone off in a strange way, so it was thrown away.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods that are sold have been disposed of to a buyer.

clue.text: They are invariably spotted as pro deals crookedly

indicators.note: crookedly means dishonestly or out of line, so the letters of pro deals are reshuffled

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Professionals are always caught when they do crooked deals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spotted' reads as being caught out; it means having spots, as a leopard never changes them.
explanation.definitionFit: Leopards have spotted coats from birth, and proverbially can never change their spots.

clue.text: Make big effort, taking son to school

indicators.note: to here means attached to, so the son letter is placed before the school word

parts.note: to school someone is to train them

explanation.surface: A parent makes a great effort to get their son to school.
explanation.definitionFit: To strain is to exert oneself to the limit, pushing hard.

clue.text: Mischief-maker, ringleader, and one child put in jail

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous little devil
the leading letter of ring
a son is a male child

explanation.surface: A troublemaker, the gang's ringleader and a child are all locked up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ringleader' reads as the gang boss, but it gives only the first letter of ring.
explanation.definitionFit: To imprison someone is to lock them up in a jail.

clue.text: Authorise possible instruction for shock treatment

definitions.meaning: first meaning: as a verb, to allow officially
second meaning, read as two words: an order to curl a shock of hair

explanation.walkthrough: Shock treatment suggests electric therapy, but a shock is a mass of hair, and the instruction is to give it a perm.
explanation.definitionFit: To permit is to give authority or consent for something to happen.

clue.text: Male with corrupt lawyer in East producing collective frenzy

indicators.note: in places the lawyer word inside the East word

parts.note: Asia is the continent of the East
a shyster is an unscrupulous lawyer

explanation.surface: A man and a crooked lawyer in the Orient spark a wave of panic.
explanation.definitionFit: Mass hysteria is irrational panic or excitement that spreads through a whole group of people.

clue.text: Polish tiny moving bits in old timepiece

definitions.meaning: first meaning: as a verb, to smooth with abrasive paper

definitions.text: tiny moving bits in old timepiece
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the grains that run through an hourglass

explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' looks like the nationality but is the verb to smooth.
explanation.definitionFit: To sand is to rub smooth with sandpaper, and sand is what trickles through an hourglass.

clue.text: Sticky wicket set up for spinners

indicators.note: in a down answer, set up means raised from bottom to top, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a sticky wicket is a tricky situation, a tight spot

explanation.surface: A cricket pitch drying awkwardly, prepared to suit the spin bowlers.
explanation.walkthrough: A sticky wicket is a cricket pitch that makes batting hard, and by extension any tight spot; spinners are slow bowlers, but here spinning toys.
explanation.definitionFit: Tops are spinning toys, set whirling on a point.

clue.text: Spell for beginner in Hamlet, ironically, rather than petty role

indicators.note: in tells us the answer lies within the words that follow, across their boundary

parts.note: the words that conceal the answer

explanation.surface: A novice actor gets a stint in Hamlet, ironically, instead of a small part.
explanation.walkthrough: The theatrical surface is padding round the hidden word; a spell is a stint.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiro, also spelt tyro, is a novice or learner.

clue.text: Smuggler on horse who's behind one?

parts.note: a runner is a smuggler, as in a gun-runner
a jockey is up when mounted

explanation.surface: A smuggler on horseback asks who is following.
explanation.walkthrough: A jockey riding a horse is said to be up.
explanation.definitionFit: The runner-up finishes second, just behind the winner.

clue.text: Person who pokes fun at flower-girl in street

indicators.note: in puts the at-plus-flower letters inside the street abbreviation

parts.note: taken as written
Iris is both a flower and a girl's name

explanation.surface: Someone mocks a girl selling flowers in the street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pokes fun at' looks like one phrase, but 'at' belongs to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A satirist ridicules people and institutions through mockery and irony.
